Settings menu design (render/settings.ts + render/audio.ts). A centered panel (getTexture('panel.settings'), 320x400) over a dark overlay, with a gear icon (getTexture('icon.gear')) beside a "SETTINGS" title, and a BACK button (getTexture('button.back')) at the bottom that plays audioManager.playSound('sfx.back') and returns to the previous screen.

Rows, top to bottom:
1. MUSIC toggle — ON/OFF, getTexture('toggle.on')/('toggle.off'); plays sfx.toggle on change; audioManager.setMusicEnabled(bool).
2. SFX toggle — ON/OFF, same toggle sprites; plays sfx.toggle on change.
3. VIBRATION toggle — ON/OFF, same toggle sprites; plays sfx.toggle on change.
4. MUSIC VOLUME slider — a draggable volume slider (SEPARATE from SFX).
5. SFX VOLUME slider — a draggable volume slider (SEPARATE from music).

VOLUME SLIDERS (the focus of this spec) — there are TWO independent sliders, one for music and one for sfx (NOT a single master volume):
- Each slider row = a label ("MUSIC VOL" / "SFX VOL"), a track Sprite getTexture('slider.track') (200x16), and a draggable knob Sprite getTexture('slider.knob') (20x28) positioned on the track.
- The knob is draggable (pointerdown on the knob -> pointermove drags -> pointerup releases; clamp the knob x to the track ends). The knob's x position along the track maps to a volume value in [0,1] (left edge = 0, right edge = 1).
- On drag, update the value live and persist it: localStorage 'rs_setting_music_vol' for the music slider and 'rs_setting_sfx_vol' for the sfx slider (store the float 0..1). Load these on show()/init and place each knob to reflect the saved value (default music 0.5, sfx 0.6).
- Music slider changes call audioManager.setMusicVolume(v); SFX slider changes call audioManager.setSfxVolume(v). Optionally play sfx.toggle (a soft tick) on sfx-slider release so the user hears the level.

AUDIO WIRING (render/audio.ts) — the AudioManager ALREADY has separate _musicGain and _sfxGain GainNodes:
- Add setMusicVolume(v: number): clamp v to [0,1] and set this._musicGain.gain.value = v (guard null ctx).
- Add setSfxVolume(v: number): clamp v to [0,1] and set this._sfxGain.gain.value = v (guard null ctx).
- When the AudioContext is first created (_getCtx), initialise _musicGain/_sfxGain from the persisted 'rs_setting_music_vol'/'rs_setting_sfx_vol' (falling back to the current defaults 0.5 / 0.6) so a saved volume applies on boot.

Character-select v2 — overhaul the EXISTING character-select screen (src/render/charselect.ts) and REMOVE the obsolete Fort Condor test character roster. Make the targeted changes below; the screen already exists, so DO NOT rebuild from scratch. Keep the deterministic gate green: do NOT edit game/test/** or game/accept/**. Render code may use performance.now(); src/sim/** must never use Math.random/Date.now/performance.now (sim-purity).

ROSTER CLEANUP (remove obsolete test artifacts):
- The characters 'granbruf', 'widowlancer', 'heajri' and the unlock system tied to them are OBSOLETE test cruft from an earlier project and are NOT part of the design. REMOVE every reference to them:
  - src/main.ts: the startRun() per-character weapon/HP/speed switch on localStorage 'rs_selected_character', AND the 'rs_unlocked_characters' unlock + migration logic (the widowlancer/heajri unlock blocks).
  - src/render/worldmap.ts: the top-left character widget's granbruf/widowlancer/heajri strings + emojis in _updateCharWidget() and the default charNameText/charAvatarText.
- The ONLY character roster is the three placeholders already on the character-select screen: Warrior (id 'a', getTexture('player.charsel_a')), Ranger (id 'b', getTexture('player.charsel_b')), Mage (id 'c', getTexture('player.charsel_c')).
- In worldmap.ts, keep a small character widget but make it show the CURRENTLY SELECTED placeholder (Warrior/Ranger/Mage by the saved id) and still open the character-select screen on tap ('Tap to change'). No granbruf/widowlancer/heajri anywhere.

MAKE THE SELECT BUTTON FUNCTIONAL:
- On SELECT press, persist the choice: localStorage.setItem('rs_selected_character', the selected id 'a'|'b'|'c'), then leave the screen via the screen's confirm/back callback (main.ts wires it to worldMap.show()). Replace the current onSelectConfirmed no-op (console.log) with this.
- startRun() (main.ts) maps the selected placeholder id to a simple loadout using EXISTING sim weapons only (do NOT invent sim content): 'a' Warrior -> weapon 'axe', maxHp 300, speed 220; 'b' Ranger -> 'knives', maxHp 250, speed 260; 'c' Mage -> 'fireball', maxHp 200, speed 180. Default to 'a' when unset.
- On show(), pre-highlight the currently-saved character (read 'rs_selected_character', default 'a').

UI IMPROVEMENTS (src/render/charselect.ts):
- TITLE: a centered 'CHOOSE YOUR HERO' title (code Text) near the top, filling the currently-empty upper area.
- BIGGER + GROUNDED: render the three character sprites noticeably LARGER (renderScale ~2.5-3x) and add a soft dark elliptical ground shadow (code Graphics, low alpha) under each so they don't float.
- NAME LABELS: show each character's name (WARRIOR / RANGER / MAGE) under its sprite at ALL times, not only when selected.
- FIRE GLOW: add getTexture('fx.charsel_fireglow') as a soft warm glow centered on the campfire (behind it, gentle pulse synced to the fire frames), casting a light pool over the nearby characters. Use a normal or additive blend.
- EMBERS: a few small rising ember motes near the fire (code-drawn small Graphics dots that drift up and fade, driven by the frame counter — render-only, performance.now is fine here).
- SELECT LABEL: when enabled, the button reads 'SELECT - <NAME>' (e.g. 'SELECT - WARRIOR'); keep the disabled(grey) -> enabled(green) states.
- INFO PANEL: keep the name + description and ALSO show a stats line (HP / SPEED / weapon) from the loadout above.
- KEYBOARD: Left/Right arrows move the selection among the three characters; Enter confirms (same as SELECT); Escape returns to the world map.

ACCEPTANCE (verified visually via snapshot, no sim test): the screen shows a title, three larger shadowed characters around a glowing campfire with a few drifting embers, and always-visible names; selecting a character (click or arrow+Enter) shows the gold highlight + an info panel with its stats, and the SELECT button reads 'SELECT - <NAME>' in its green enabled state; NO references to granbruf / widowlancer / heajri remain anywhere in main.ts or worldmap.ts.

Deterministic parabola: this is a projectile with GRAVITY. Add OPTIONAL field `gravity?: number` to the Projectile interface (px/s^2 downward). Add a spawnArcingProj helper (or extend spawn) that sets an initial upward velocity (vy negative, e.g. vy = -300) plus some horizontal velocity toward nearest (vx = nx * 150) and proj.gravity = a positive constant (e.g. 600). Add a new WeaponBehavior 'arc'. Its branch spawns ONE arcing projectile. The hammer damages enemies on contact like a normal projectile (reuse the existing hit path) and despawns at maxRange or when it exits the arena / reaches a bottom bound (you may despawn on maxRange as the existing loop does). Because gravity accumulates on vy, the path is a deterministic parabola. Ensure gravity is reset (to undefined/0) for non-arc spawns so a reused pool slot does not keep falling. cooldown ~1.4, baseDamage ~55 (heavy).

3. FLAIL — id 'flail', name 'Flail', rarity 'common'. GDD: a rotating spiky ball ORBITING the character, dealing CONSTANT contact damage each tick to enemies it touches. This is NOT a projectile — it is a persistent orbiting hitbox. Deterministic orbit driven by sim TIME (s.time), not wall clock. Model it as sim state on the player or GameState: since the flail exists only while equipped, drive its position from s.time and the slot: add a new WeaponBehavior 'orbit'. Then damage every enemy within (ballRadius ~20 + enemy.radius) of (bx,by) THIS tick: apply damageForLevel(def, level) * FIXED_DT as a per-tick contact tick (so damage-per-second is roughly baseDamage), collect-then-kill, and count these AoE-style hits toward s.weaponAoeFires if you want the AoE counter to reflect it (optional). Because the flail applies damage every tick while overlapping, use a per-tick fractional damage (baseDamage scaled by FIXED_DT) rather than full baseDamage per tick, so it reads as a continuous contact weapon. To support MULTIPLE flails or duplicate slots, offset each additional flail's angle by (PI * slotIndexAmongFlails) so they orbit opposite each other — deterministic. Note: because the flail's cooldown-timer firing model does not fit (it is continuous), you may either (a) keep a nominal cooldown in the WeaponDef but IGNORE it for orbit (drive purely from s.time), or (b) fire the orbit tick every frame from a separate loop over orbit-weapons — approach (b) is cleaner. Keep the WeaponDef.cooldown at a nominal value (~1.0) for schema consistency even if unused by the orbit path. baseDamage ~120 (this is DPS-per-second before the FIXED_DT scaling). Ensure this continuous path stays deterministic: angle from s.time only, enemy iteration via forEachActive (ordered).

This is the ONE weapon that legitimately uses rng — and it MUST use state.rng, never Math.random. Add a new WeaponBehavior 'acid-throw'. Its branch: pick a RANDOM active enemy using state.rng (e.g. count active enemies, r = s.rng.int(0, count), select the r-th in forEachActive order — deterministic given the seed), then place a puddle near that enemy at an rng-jittered offset: px = enemy.x + s.rng.range(-30, 30), py = enemy.y + s.rng.range(-30, 30); push { id: s.nextId++, x:px, y:py, radius ~70, remaining ~3.0 (seconds), dps = damageForLevel(def, level) } onto s.acidPuddles. If there are no active enemies, do nothing (skip, reset timer to fire next tick as the existing !hasTarget guard does — note: acid needs a target too, so the existing hasTarget guard is fine). Add a puddle-tick pass in weaponSystem (or a small helper called from it): for each puddle, remaining -= FIXED_DT; damage every enemy within radius by dps * FIXED_DT (per-tick fraction), collect-then-kill; also damage destructibles similarly; increment s.weaponAoeFires when a puddle deals damage (optional but lets AoE tests observe it). Remove puddles whose remaining <= 0 (filter the array once after the pass, like telegraphs are filtered in loop.ts). All rng calls MUST be s.rng.* — this keeps determinism (same seed => same puddle placement). cooldown ~2.2, baseDamage ~30 (as puddle dps).

If you add fields, make sure makeProjectile()/reset paths don't leave stale gravity on reused slots.

assets.instructions:
GOAL: Add the two TRIGGER-ON-HIT (reactive) GDD weapons — Tower Shield and Smoke Bomb — to Realm Survivors (Cosmo Canyon Ready Spec; Vite + TS + PixiJS v8, deterministic sim + Pixi renderer). Unlike every other weapon, these do NOT fire on a per-slot cooldown timer; they fire when the PLAYER TAKES DAMAGE, and each has a long cooldown shown on the player.

IMPORTANT PATH CORRECTIONS: The `files` list uses shorthands. The real files are: weapon DATA = src/sim/data/weapons.ts; weapon FIRE LOGIC = src/sim/systems/weapons.ts (NOT src/sim/weapons.ts); player-damage / combat = src/sim/systems/combat.ts (NOT src/sim/combat.ts); renderer = src/render/stage.ts; HUD = src/render/hud.ts. Note there are MULTIPLE places the player takes damage: (1) enemy CONTACT damage in src/sim/systems/combat.ts (combatSystem), (2) telegraph AoE damage in src/sim/loop.ts (runTick, the telegraph pass), and (3) boss/mini-boss projectiles in src/sim/systems/boss-attack.ts (if it damages the player there). To make the trigger fire on ALL damage sources, centralize player damage through ONE helper (see below) rather than hooking each site separately.

HARD RULES (must obey):
- NEVER edit game/test/** or game/accept/** — tamper-guarded. Keep the EXISTING gate green (tsc + existing tests: test/determinism.ts, test/sim-purity.ts, test/sim.weapons.ts, test/sim.win-loss.ts, test/sim.boss.ts).
- src/sim/** deterministic: NO Math.random / Date.now / performance.now / requestAnimationFrame under src/sim/. Reactive cooldowns MUST count down via FIXED_DT (seconds), never wall-clock. Randomness (if any) = seeded state.rng only. test/sim-purity.ts hard-fails on the four banned APIs. src/render/** may use performance.now.
- test/sim.weapons.ts rarity loop asserts: bomb-kunai/viking-spread/fire-axe => 'rare'; ragnarok/infinite-kunai/god-spread => 'legendary'; EVERY OTHER id => 'common'. CRITICAL: set rarity of BOTH new weapons ('tower-shield', 'smoke-bomb') to 'common' so the loop stays green without editing tests.
- maxLevel stays literal 3. Placeholder art only; new fx.* keys auto-declare via getTexture() (src/assets/registry.ts).
- DETERMINISM OF THE DAMAGE-NEGATION SEMANTICS matters: test/sim.win-loss.ts and test/determinism.ts run the default loadout (no shield/smoke equipped by default — player starts with only 'axe'), so the DEFAULT runs must be byte-identical. Only change player-damage behavior when the reactive weapon is EQUIPPED and OFF cooldown. Do NOT alter default damage math.

SHAPES YOU EXTEND (read first): src/sim/systems/combat.ts (combatSystem applies contact damage `p.hp -= dps * FIXED_DT` and sets p.alive=false / outcome='loss' when hp<=0; killEnemy; dist2). src/sim/loop.ts (telegraph pass subtracts t.damage from p.hp). src/sim/systems/boss-attack.ts (boss projectile player hits, if any). src/sim/state.ts (GameState, Player{...,weapons}, EquippedWeapon{weaponId,level,timer,rarity?}, enemyProjectiles pool, newGame(), snapshot()). src/sim/systems/weapons.ts (addWeapon, weaponSystem, spawnProj, triggerExplosion). src/render/hud.ts (HUD class draws hp/xp bars + stats + timer + boss text; sync(s,screenW,screenH)). src/render/stage.ts (Renderer.sync draws player, glow, overlays).

ARCHITECTURE — CENTRALIZE PLAYER DAMAGE (do this first): Add an exported deterministic helper `applyPlayerDamage(s: GameState, amount: number, opts?: { source?: 'contact' | 'telegraph' | 'projectile' }): void` (put it in src/sim/systems/combat.ts and export it; import where needed). This helper is the single choke point where reactive weapons intercept damage. Its logic:
  1. If amount <= 0 or !s.player.alive, return.
  2. TOWER SHIELD: if the player has an equipped weapon with weaponId 'tower-shield' AND its reactive cooldown is 0 (ready): NEGATE this damage entirely (do NOT subtract from hp), start the shield cooldown (45s), and TRIGGER the shield effect (see below). Return WITHOUT applying damage. (Shield negates exactly ONE hit, then goes on cooldown for 45s.)
  3. SMOKE BOMB: if the player has 'smoke-bomb' equipped AND its cooldown is 0 (ready): this does NOT negate the triggering damage by default (GDD says brief invincibility + AoE damage). Apply the triggering damage normally (step 4) BUT then start a short INVULN window and the 30s cooldown and trigger the smoke AoE. During the invuln window, applyPlayerDamage should return early (negate) for its duration. (So smoke-bomb reduces incoming damage during the brief window after a hit, and damages nearby enemies.)
  4. Otherwise subtract: s.player.hp -= amount; if s.player.hp <= 0 { hp = 0; alive = false; outcome = 'loss' }.
Then REPLACE the direct `p.hp -= ...` writes at the three damage sites with calls to applyPlayerDamage(s, dmgAmount, {source}): (a) in combatSystem, the contact-damage line becomes applyPlayerDamage(s, dps * FIXED_DT, {source:'contact'}); (b) in loop.ts telegraph pass, `p.hp -= t.damage` becomes applyPlayerDamage(s, t.damage, {source:'telegraph'}); (c) in boss-attack.ts if it deducts player hp, route it through applyPlayerDamage(...,{source:'projectile'}). IMPORTANT: keep the EXACT same numeric result for the default loadout (no shield/smoke) — applyPlayerDamage's step 4 must reproduce the current behavior byte-for-byte (same subtraction, same <=0 -> alive=false/outcome='loss'), so determinism.ts and win-loss.ts stay green. Contact damage is a per-tick fraction (dps*FIXED_DT); note that routing tiny fractional hits through the shield would waste the negate on a 0.13-hp tick. To make the shield meaningful, ONLY treat a hit as a 'shield-worthy hit' when source is 'telegraph' or 'projectile' (discrete burst hits), OR when amount >= a threshold (e.g. >= 5). For 'contact' fractional damage below the threshold, skip the shield/smoke trigger and just apply normally. Document this threshold in a comment. (This keeps determinism intact and matches the GDD intent of negating a real hit, not a sliver of contact damage.)

NEW SIM STATE (src/sim/state.ts): add reactive cooldown + invuln fields to GameState (NOT per-slot, since these are singleton effects; 'only one copy of each Tier-1 weapon at a time' per the GDD): add `towerShieldCooldown: number` (seconds remaining; 0 = ready), `smokeBombCooldown: number` (0 = ready), and `smokeInvuln: number` (seconds of active invulnerability remaining; 0 = none). Initialize all three to 0 in newGame(). Add constants (e.g. near the other tuning consts in state.ts): TOWER_SHIELD = { cooldown: 45, aoeRadiusX: 140, aoeRadiusY: 70, knockback: 200, damage: <choose, e.g. 40> }; SMOKE_BOMB = { cooldown: 30, invulnDuration: 1.0, aoeRadius: 120, damage: <e.g. 60> }. Decrement the cooldowns and invuln every tick by FIXED_DT (clamp at 0) — do this in a small pass in weaponSystem or a dedicated reactiveCooldownSystem called from loop.ts; deterministic (FIXED_DT only, no wall clock).

TOWER SHIELD EFFECT (triggered from applyPlayerDamage when shield fires): (1) negate the damage (already handled), (2) set s.towerShieldCooldown = TOWER_SHIELD.cooldown, (3) do a HORIZONTAL OVAL AoE in FRONT of the player that (a) damages + KNOCKS BACK enemies and (b) DEFLECTS enemy projectiles. Implement as an instant effect: define the oval region in front of the player. 'In front' — the game auto-targets nearest; use the direction toward the nearest enemy (compute nearest like weaponSystem does) as 'front', or if no target use a default facing (e.g. up: (0,-1)). Oval test: for each active enemy, transform (e - player) into the aim frame and test (localX/aoeRadiusX)^2 + (localY/aoeRadiusY)^2 <= 1; if inside: e.hp -= TOWER_SHIELD.damage (collect-then-kill via killEnemy), and apply KNOCKBACK by pushing the enemy position away from the player along (e-player) normalized by TOWER_SHIELD.knockback px (adjust e.x/e.y directly — deterministic). DEFLECT projectiles: iterate s.enemyProjectiles.forEachActive; for any enemy projectile inside the same oval, REVERSE its velocity (vx = -vx; vy = -vy) OR release it from the pool (deflect = remove is simplest and deterministic) — prefer reversing velocity so it visually flies back; ensure this does not damage the player afterward. Increment s.weaponAoeFires so the effect is observable. All deterministic, no rng.

SMOKE BOMB EFFECT (triggered from applyPlayerDamage when smoke fires): (1) set s.smokeBombCooldown = SMOKE_BOMB.cooldown, (2) set s.smokeInvuln = SMOKE_BOMB.invulnDuration (grants brief invulnerability — applyPlayerDamage returns early/negates while smokeInvuln > 0), (3) instant AoE: damage every enemy within SMOKE_BOMB.aoeRadius of the PLAYER by SMOKE_BOMB.damage (collect-then-kill, hit destructibles too), increment s.weaponAoeFires. Deterministic. Note ordering: the triggering hit's own damage is applied normally BEFORE the invuln window starts (per GDD 'on being hit'), then subsequent hits within the ~1s window are negated.

WEAPON DEFS (src/sim/data/weapons.ts): add two WeaponDefs to WEAPON_POOL: { id:'tower-shield', name:'Tower Shield', cooldown:45, behavior:'reactive', baseDamage: <TOWER_SHIELD.damage e.g.40>, maxLevel:3, rarity:'common' } and { id:'smoke-bomb', name:'Smoke Bomb', cooldown:30, behavior:'reactive', baseDamage:<SMOKE_BOMB.damage e.g.60>, maxLevel:3, rarity:'common' }. Add a new WeaponBehavior string 'reactive' to the union. In weaponSystem's per-slot fire loop, the 'reactive' behavior must be a NO-OP on the cooldown-timer path (these weapons do NOT fire on the slot timer) — add `else if (def.behavior === 'reactive') { /* triggered on player-hit, not on timer */ }` so the timer branch does nothing (or `continue` before firing for reactive slots). This prevents them from spawning projectiles every cooldown. The reactive cooldown decrement (towerShieldCooldown/smokeBombCooldown/smokeInvuln) is separate from slot.timer.

HUD / STAGE — SHOW COOLDOWN ON THE PLAYER (src/render/hud.ts and/or src/render/stage.ts): The GDD requires the reactive cooldown be VISIBLE ON THE CHARACTER. Preferred: in src/render/stage.ts Renderer.sync, if the player has 'tower-shield' equipped, draw a small cooldown indicator AT the player position (world space) — e.g. a ring/arc around the player whose fill = 1 - (s.towerShieldCooldown / 45) so it sweeps to full as it recharges, using fx.tower_shield or a colored arc; when ready (cooldown 0) show a subtle 'ready' glow. Same for 'smoke-bomb' with fx.smoke_bomb and /30. Additionally (optional, easier) show a text/pip in the HUD (src/render/hud.ts) listing each reactive weapon and its remaining cooldown seconds (e.g. 'Shield 12s' / 'Smoke ready'). Access s.towerShieldCooldown / s.smokeBombCooldown / equipped weapons from GameState in hud.sync / stage.sync. Render code may read these sim fields freely (render is one-way sim->view). Keep the player-anchored indicator in WORLD space (added to this.world or drawn relative to player.x/player.y) so it sits on the character, per GDD.

fx TEXTURES: Tower Shield -> fx.tower_shield; Smoke Bomb -> fx.smoke_bomb. Reference both in stage.ts (and/or as HUD icons) so the keys declare and appear in the wishlist; they render as labeled grey-box placeholders until real art exists — acceptable.

DETERMINISM / ACCEPTANCE (NO test/** edits — satisfy the existing gate + describe checks):
- Both new weapons rarity 'common' => test/sim.weapons.ts rarity loop stays green.
- DEFAULT loadout unchanged: applyPlayerDamage step 4 must reproduce current damage math EXACTLY, so test/determinism.ts (1200 ticks x2) and test/sim.win-loss.ts (player must still die/lose under swarm pressure with the default axe-only loadout) stay green. Verify by running the gate after refactoring the three damage sites through applyPlayerDamage — the numbers must not move for a run with no shield/smoke equipped. New GameState fields (towerShieldCooldown/smokeBombCooldown/smokeInvuln) init to 0 and are deterministic, so adding them to snapshot() (optional, for observability) is safe (determinism.ts compares run-A vs run-B, not a golden file).
- Self-verify with a THROWAWAY gitignored scratch script (game/.claude/scratch/ or scratch_*.ts; delete before finishing): (a) TOWER SHIELD — newGame; set player.weapons=[{weaponId:'tower-shield',level:1,timer:0}]; place an enemy so it deals a discrete hit OR directly call applyPlayerDamage(s, 30, {source:'projectile'}); assert the FIRST such hit is NEGATED (player.hp unchanged) AND s.towerShieldCooldown becomes 45 AND s.weaponAoeFires increased (oval fired); then call applyPlayerDamage again immediately and assert the SECOND hit IS applied (hp drops) because the shield is on cooldown; tick ~45s of FIXED_DT and assert cooldown returns to 0 and negation works again. Also spawn an enemy projectile inside the oval and assert its velocity reversed (deflection). (b) SMOKE BOMB — set player.weapons=[{weaponId:'smoke-bomb',...}]; surround the player with enemies; call applyPlayerDamage(s, 30, {source:'projectile'}); assert the triggering hit applied normally, s.smokeBombCooldown became 30, s.smokeInvuln > 0, nearby enemies took damage (weaponAoeFires up / enemies died); then within the invuln window call applyPlayerDamage again and assert it is negated; after invuln expires assert damage applies again. Confirm TWO identical-seed runs of each scenario produce identical results (no rng). Delete the scratch file. Permanent proof: tsc + existing tests green.

Equip Tower Shield: on the first hit, a horizontal oval flashes in front of the player, nearby enemies get shoved back, enemy projectiles bounce, and a cooldown ring appears on the character counting down ~45s. Equip Smoke Bomb: on a hit, a smoke burst flashes around the player, nearby enemies take damage, the player is briefly untouchable, and a ~30s cooldown shows on the character. fx.tower_shield / fx.smoke_bomb render as labeled grey placeholders — acceptable. No console errors, no crash, and the default game (no reactive weapon equipped) plays exactly as before.

The real draft/upgrade logic lives in `src/sim/systems/upgrades.ts` (re-exported through `src/sim/index.ts`). Edit `src/sim/systems/upgrades.ts` wherever these instructions say 'the upgrades system'. Do NOT create a new `src/sim/upgrades.ts`.

GOAL: Add an on-screen virtual joystick VISUAL for the existing touch/mouse-drag movement. Realm Survivors is a vertical mobile game: press finger + drag moves the character in that direction; release stops. The movement math already works (src/render/input.ts InputManager.readInput produces a normalized {dx,dy} from a drag) and is already fed to the sim in src/main.ts. This spec ONLY adds the joystick graphic that shows the base at the touch point and a knob that follows the finger. Do NOT change the move vector the sim receives, and do NOT touch any sim file.

HARD RULES (must hold): NEVER edit game/test/** or game/accept/**. src/render/** is render-only and MAY use performance.now and navigator APIs, but MUST NOT be imported by src/sim/**. Do not add Math.random. Keep the gate green (npm run gate / the project's build+test). Placeholder art is acceptable — getTexture(key) returns a labeled grey box immediately and swaps in real art asynchronously, so just use the keys.

AVAILABLE ASSET KEYS (already Ready-seeded; call getTexture with them exactly): ui.joystick_base (96x96), ui.joystick_knob (48x48). Note: these keys may not yet be present in assets/manifest.json — that is fine, getTexture(key) auto-declares a placeholder for unknown keys and never throws. Use them directly.

CURRENT STATE TO GROUND ON:
- src/render/input.ts InputManager: fields startX/startY (pointer-down point, clientX/clientY), currentX/currentY (latest drag point), isDragging, deadzone=8, activePointerId. readInput(active) returns keyboard first, else the drag vector (dx/dy)/dist when dist>deadzone. Movement is pointer-based on the whole window.
- src/render/stage.ts Renderer: a Pixi v8 Application with a world Container (camera-translated to center the player) and an app.stage. HUD overlay lives above the world. The camera sets this.world.x/y each sync(). getTexture/getEntry imported from ../assets/registry.

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. In src/render/input.ts, expose read-only accessors so the renderer can draw the joystick without duplicating pointer state. Add public getters (or a single public method) that return: whether a touch/mouse drag is currently active (isDragging AND the vector exceeds deadzone is NOT required for showing the base — show the base as soon as isDragging is true), the SCREEN-space anchor point (startX, startY in clientX/clientY pixels), and the current drag point (currentX, currentY). Example public API to add: `get dragActive(): boolean { return this.isDragging; }`, `get dragStart(): {x:number,y:number} { return { x: this.startX, y: this.startY }; }`, `get dragCurrent(): {x:number,y:number} { return { x: this.currentX, y: this.currentY }; }`. Do NOT change onPointerDown/Move/Up or readInput math — only add getters. The joystick must NOT interfere with WASD: WASD still works because readInput checks keyboard first; the joystick visual is only shown while a pointer drag is active.
2. In src/render/stage.ts, add a SCREEN-SPACE (NOT world-space) joystick overlay so it does not scroll with the camera. Add two Sprites: a base sprite from getTexture('ui.joystick_base') (96x96, anchor 0.5,0.5) and a knob sprite from getTexture('ui.joystick_knob') (48x48, anchor 0.5,0.5). Add them to app.stage (the same layer as the HUD/overlay, ABOVE this.world) so their coordinates are raw screen pixels, not camera-translated. Start both invisible.
3. Give the Renderer a way to receive the input state. Simplest: add a method `syncJoystick(input: { dragActive: boolean; dragStart: {x:number;y:number}; dragCurrent: {x:number;y:number} }): void` on Renderer, and call it from src/main.ts each frame right after computing input (in the ticker, near where inputManager.readInput is used). Pass the InputManager's new getters. In syncJoystick: if !dragActive, set base.visible=false and knob.visible=false and return. Otherwise set base.visible=true, base.x=dragStart.x, base.y=dragStart.y. Compute the knob offset = (dragCurrent - dragStart); clamp its length to a KNOB_RADIUS (use 48, i.e. half the 96 base). If length>KNOB_RADIUS scale the offset to KNOB_RADIUS. Set knob.visible=true, knob.x = dragStart.x + clampedOffsetX, knob.y = dragStart.y + clampedOffsetY. Re-pull getTexture('ui.joystick_base')/('ui.joystick_knob') each call and reassign sprite.texture only if it changed (mirror the placeholder→real async-swap pattern already used elsewhere in stage.ts, e.g. `if (spr.texture !== tex) spr.texture = tex;`), and re-set width/height=96/96 and 48/48 respectively so the async real art keeps the intended size.
4. IMPORTANT — the base+knob offset MUST match the SAME direction/magnitude convention the sim already uses: the drag vector fed to the sim is (currentX-startX, currentY-startY) normalized. The knob offset uses the same (current-start) delta (just clamped for display), so the knob visually points where the character moves. Do not invert Y. Do not recompute movement here — the sim vector still comes only from InputManager.readInput in main.ts.
5. Hide the joystick whenever movement input is not active (release → onPointerUp sets isDragging=false → dragActive false → hidden). Also ensure it stays hidden on menus: main.ts already gates stepping behind menu/levelup visibility; only call syncJoystick with a live drag during actual play, or simply rely on dragActive being false when inputManager.cancelDrag() has run (it is called on menus/level-up). Calling syncJoystick unconditionally is fine because dragActive will be false when not dragging.

VERIFICATION (visual, via the preview snapshot harness): start the app, begin a run, simulate a pointer-down + drag in the play area (dispatch pointerdown then pointermove events, or use the preview eval to set InputManager drag state), force a render (window.__render()), and screenshot. Expect the joystick base centered at the touch point with the knob offset toward the drag direction, clamped within the base radius. On pointer-up the joystick disappears. Confirm WASD still moves the player (keyboard path unaffected). Do not regress the gate.

DESIGN RULES — operator rulings 2026-07-04 (STANDING AUTHORITY; supersedes any older spec text that conflicts)

These are binding design constraints for Realm Survivors (cosmo-canyon/game). They correct prototype
bleed-through. Planners: treat these as invariants — do NOT mint tasks that violate them.

1. NO WEAPON FUSION in this version. Fusion (fuseWeapons, FUSION_RECIPES, fusion draft cards) is
   prototype legacy. It must NEVER be offered in real-game drafts (a party pool is always set in real
   runs; the code already excludes it there). The sim/test vestiges stay ONLY because protected headless
   tests exercise them. If fusion ever returns, it will be designed as a NEW CHARACTER'S META-MECHANIC —
   not a generic draft option. Do not re-wire it into drafts, chests, or UI.

2. TIER-1 WEAPON COVERAGE. Every Tier-1 weapon must (a) appear in at least one character's weaponPool and
   (b) have an evolution path terminating in at least one Tier-3 form. Current chains (complete):
   axe, knives, fireball(->greater-fireball->cataclysm), shuriken, wand-of-fireball, throwing-knives,
   javelin, crossbow, greatsword, holy-symbol, whip, throwing-hammer, flail, acid-potion,
   tower-shield(->aegis-wall->bulwark-eternal), smoke-bomb(->nightshade-bomb->oblivion-veil),
   magic-missile, chain-lightning, frost-shard, sky-strike, arcane-nova, toxic-cloud, curse-skull,
   seismic-slam. Reactive-family evolutions trigger via family lists in combat.ts with tier-scaled damage.
   When adding a NEW weapon: give it a pool slot + a full evolution chain, mark it partyOnly:true
   (determinism rail — see docs/KNOWLEDGE.md), rarity 'common'.

3. ROGUE POISON BOMB = ENEMY DROP. Poison bombs drop from slain normal enemies (POISON_BOMB.dropChance
   roll in combat.killEnemy, gated on rogueInParty). There is NO ambient/timed spawn. The older
   poison_bomb_pickup.txt spec describing a 12s timer cadence is RETIRED — its throw-on-pickup + cloud
   behavior remains valid; only the spawn mechanism changed.

4. FUSION-ONLY OUTPUTS (bomb-kunai, viking-spread, fire-axe, ragnarok, infinite-kunai, god-spread) are
   NOT part of this version's real-game content. They stay defined for the protected tests only. Do not
   add them to character pools or drafts.
